key_insight: WeightBench shows that frontier LLMs can interpret small neural networks and write working control policies directly in weight space, but struggle with harder model edits.
engineering_relevance: Weight-space programming could enable gradient-free model inspection and modification, but current capabilities do not reliably extend to language-model patching or data-free compression.
method: Evaluate 42 tasks across weight reading, fixing, writing, impossible-edit recognition, and data-free compression.
Test networks ranging from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models.
Provide a public task registry, OS-level sandbox harness, code, and live leaderboard.
evidence_signal: Opus 5.5 scores 0.535 across all 42 tasks; on the 38-task subset evaluated for GPT-6.1-sol, GPT scores 0.568 versus Opus's 0.546.
watch_item: Agents cannot yet reliably distinguish impossible edits from difficult ones, making feasibility checks essential before deployment.
paper_title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
